questions.question: A and B together can finish a job in 20 days. B and C together can finish the same job in 30 days. If A and C together can finish it in 24 days, in how many days can A alone finish the job?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B = 20 days

B and C = 30 days

A and C = 24 days

**Formula used:**

Total work = LCM of days

Efficiency = Total work / Days

**Calculation:**

LCM of 20, 30, and 24 = 120 units

Efficiency of A and B = 120 / 20 = 6 units/day

Efficiency of B and C = 120 / 30 = 4 units/day

Efficiency of A and C = 120 / 24 = 5 units/day

Adding all efficiencies:

(A + B) + (B + C) + (A + C) = 6 + 4 + 5

2(A + B + C) = 15

A + B + C = 15 / 2 = 7.5 units/day

Efficiency of A = (A + B + C) - (B + C)

Efficiency of A = 7.5 - 4 = 3.5 units/day

Days taken by A alone = Total work / Efficiency of A

Days taken by A alone = 120 / 3.5

Days taken by A alone = 1200 / 35

Days taken by A alone = 240 / 7

Days taken by A alone = 34 ²/₇ days

**∴ A alone can finish the job in 34 ²/₇ days.**

questions.question: A boat covers a distance of 1 km against the current of the stream in half an hour and a distance of 3 km in the direction of the current in 30 minutes. How long will it take for the boat to go 8 km in still water?

Distance = Speed × Time

Upstream speed (U) = V - S

Downstream speed (D) = V + S

Where, V = Speed of boat in still water, S = Speed of current

**Calculation:**

Upstream speed (U) = 1/0.5 = 2 km/hour

⇒ V - S = 2 -----(1)

Downstream speed = 3/0.5 = 6 km/hour

⇒ V + S = 6 -----(2) 

Adding equation(1) to equation(2)

⇒ 2V = 8

⇒ V = 8/2 = 4 km/hour

So, speed of boat in still water = 4 km/hour

Time to travel 8 km in still water = 8/4 = 2 hours

**∴ Boat will go 8 km in still water in 2 hours.**

**∴ The correct answer is 13 (3).**

• **Electric field (E) at a point** is defined as the force experienced by a positive test charge (q₀) placed at that point: E = (F)/(q₀) 
 
• where:
 
 
• **(E) is the electric field strength in newtons per coulomb (N/C).**
 
• **(F) is the force experienced by the test charge.**
 
• **(q₀) is the magnitude of the test charge.**
 
 
 
• **Electric potential, on the other hand, is related to energy, not force**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Volt (V):**

 
 
• The **volt is the standard unit of electric potential difference or voltage.**
 
• It represents the amount of potential energy per unit charge.
 
• Mathematically, electric potential difference ((V)) between two points is given by: V = (W)/(q) , where:
 
• **(V) is the potential difference (voltage) in volts.**
 
• **(W) is the work done (energy) in joules.**
 
• **(q) is the charge in coulombs.**
 
• For example,** if a battery provides a potential difference of 9 volts, it means that each coulomb of charge gains 9 joules of energy when moving from the negative terminal to the positive terminal of the battery.**
 
 
 
• **Newton-Meter per Coulomb (N·m/C):**
 
 
• A Newton meter is a unit of work, which is energy transferred.
 
• **Since energy per charge (work done per unit charge) is the definition of electric potential, so Newton-meter per Coulomb is a unit of electric potential.**
 
 
 
• **Joules per Coulomb (J/C):**
 
 
• This unit is **equivalent to the volt (V).**
 
• Electric potential can be expressed in joules per coulomb or volts.
 
• The relationship between potential energy (U) and potential difference (V) is: **U = qV **where:
 
• **(U) is the potential energy in joules.**
 
• **(q) is the charge in coulombs.**
 
• **(V) is the potential difference in volts.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a Cold Ocean Current?

__
 
• **Oyashio:**

 
 
• Oyashio is a cold ocean current that flows southward along the eastern coast of the Kamchatka Peninsula and the Kuril Islands, eventually merging with the warmer Kuroshio Current off the coast of Japan.
 
• This current is known for its nutrient-rich waters, which support a diverse and abundant marine ecosystem, including fish species like salmon and pollock.
 
• The cold waters of the Oyashio Current have a significant impact on the climate of the regions it flows past, often bringing cooler temperatures and affecting local weather patterns.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Antilles:**

 
 
• The Antilles Current is a warm ocean current that flows northward to the east of the Antilles Islands in the Caribbean Sea.
 
• It is part of the larger Atlantic Ocean circulation system and contributes to the Gulf Stream.
 
 
 
• **Alaska:**
 
 
• The Alaska Current, also known as the Alaskan Stream, is a warm ocean current that flows westward along the southern coast of Alaska and the Aleutian Islands.
 
• It is a continuation of the North Pacific Current and has a significant influence on the climate of the coastal regions it flows past, bringing milder temperatures and increased precipitation.
 
 
 
• **Agulhas:**
 
 
• The Agulhas Current is a warm ocean current that flows southward along the east coast of Africa, from the Mozambique Channel to the southern tip of the continent.
 
• It is one of the fastest and strongest currents in the world and plays a crucial role in the Indian Ocean circulation system.

• Understanding the nature of ocean currents is crucial for navigation, climate studies, and marine biology.

questions.question: When was Ashoka Mehta Committee appointed to inquire into the working of Panchayati Raj Institutions and suggest measures to strengthen them?

• In **December 1977**, the **Janata Government **constituted the ***Ashok Mehta Committee ***to research Panchayati raj institutions.

 
 
• As an alternative to the tyre system suggested by the **Balwant Rai committee**, this committee promoted a two-tier structure for Panchayat Raj, incorporating Zilla Parishads at the district level and Mandal Panchayats.
 
• It produced a report in August 1978 with 132 recommendations for bolstering and revitalising the nation's failing Panchayati raj structure.
 
 
 
• **Recommendations of Ashoka Mehta Committee:**
 
 
• A district-level Zila Parishad and a Mandal panchayat made up of a group of villages with a combined population of 15,000–20,000 people should replace the current three-tier Panchayati raj system.
 
• The district should be the first stage of decentralisation under popular control below the state level.
 
• The executive body and one in charge of district planning will be the Zila Parishad.
 
• All levels of panchayat elections should permit the participation of political parties.
 
• Panchayati raj organisations must have the ability to compel taxes in order to raise their own financial resources.
 
• Social audits must be carried out on a regular basis.

 Elections must be held within six months if the Panchayati institutions are superseded.
 
• *Institutions under the Panchayati must receive constitutional status*. 
 
• The Minister of Panchayati Raj must be appointed at the state level.
 
• Seats must be reserved for candidates from SC and STs.
 
 
 
• The Ashok Mehta Committee's recommendations could not be implemented at the national level since the Janata Government fell before the conclusion of its mandate.
 
 
• However, the Ashok Mehta Committee's recommendations were partially taken into consideration by the three states of **Karnataka, West Bengal**, and **Andhra Pradesh** as they made efforts to revive the Panchayati raj.

questions.question: Which of the following forts of Rajasthan is famous for the historic event known as Dhai Sako?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaisalmer Fort**__.

__
 
• Jaisalmer Fort

 
 
• Jaisalmer Fort is famous for "Dhai Saka" (Two and a Half Sakas).
 
• The first Saka of Jaisalmer Fort occurred during Alauddin Khilji's invasion (1296-1316 AD).
 
• The second Saka occurred during Firoz Shah Tughlaq's invasion (1351-1388 AD), when Rawal Duda, Trilokasi, and other Bhati heroes were martyred in battle.
 
• The third Saka is known as "Ardhasaka" ("Half Saka") because the warriors were martyred in battle, but no Jauhar (mass self-immolation) took place.
 
• Rawal Lunakaran was martyred in 1550 AD in a battle with Amir Ali.
 
• However, since the Bhatis emerged victorious, the women did not perform Jauhar.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Gagron Fort

 
 
• In 1423 AD, Sultan Hoshangshah of Mandu attacked Gagron Fort, and the ruler of that time, Achaldas Khinchi, was martyred.
 
• The women performed Jauhar. This is known as the first Saka of Gagron.
 
• In 1444 AD, Sultan Mahmud Khilji I of Malwa captured the fort.
 
• At that time, the women of the fort performed Jauhar, which became known as the second Saka of Gagron.
 
 
 
• Ranthambore Fort
 
 
• In 1301 AD, due to the betrayal of Hammir's ministers, Alauddin Khilji succeeded in capturing Ranthambore Fort.
 
• During this time, Hammir's wife Rangdevi and daughter Deval De led the women in performing Jauhar, which is known as the first Saka of Ranthambore.
 
 
 
• **Chittorgarh Fort**
 
 
• In the eighth century, Bappa Rawal, the founder of the Guhilot dynasty, seized the fort from the last Maurya ruler, Manamori.
 
• First Saka - In 1303 AD, during the time of Alauddin Khilji, associated with the Jauhar of Padmini and the exceptional valor of Gora and Badal.
 
• Second Saka - In 1534 AD, the Jauhar of Rani Karnavati, wife of Rana Sanga, during the time of Sultan Bahadur Shah of Gujarat.
 
• Third Saka - In 1568 AD, the Jauhar of the wives of Jaimal and Fatta and the tales of their courageous sacrifice during the attack of Akbar.
 
• These are known as the three Sakas of Chittorgarh.

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.

The correct sentence is '**The strawberry shortcake tastes delicious.**'

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 2**, '**The strawberry shortcake tastes delicious**', is correct because the verb '**tastes**' is a linking verb that describes a state or condition. After linking verbs, we use adjectives, not adverbs. 'Delicious' is an adjective and fits correctly here.
 
• **Adjectives **are used to describe or **modify nouns** or **pronouns**. In this case, the adjective '**delicious**' is describing the noun '**strawberry shortcake**'.
 
• **Adverbs **("**deliciously**", in **options 1 **and** 3**) are not used after linking verbs to describe the subject. They are typically used to modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, which is not the case here.
 
• This rule applies to all senses, i.e., sight, smell, taste, hearing, and touch. So the '**taste**' as a sense should be followed by an adjective.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 4**, 'The strawberry shortcake tasting delicious.' is **incorrect **because it is not a complete sentence. It lacks a subject and a complete verb (auxiliary or main verb). "Tasting delicious" acts as a present participle phrase without a subject for it to modify.
